card_summary: Media Links has integrated JPEG XS into its MDP3020 IP media gateway. The product is designed for live signal transport. The integration of JPEG XS enables low-latency and low-bitrate video transmission, making it suitable for live production applications where signal integrity and frame-accuracy are critical, such as those using ST 2110 and NMOS for device discovery and registration.

Technical Analysis: JPEG XS Compression Reduces Latency in Live IP Broadcasts

At the recent NAB Show, intoPIX announced the integration of their JPEG XS compression technology into several live IP broadcast solutions, including those from major industry players such as EVS and Grass Valley. This development is significant as it enables the transport of high-quality, low-latency video over standard IP networks, leveraging the SMPTE ST 2110 standard for professional media over managed IP networks. The use of JPEG XS compression is particularly noteworthy for its ability to reduce the bitrate of video signals without compromising quality, making it an attractive solution for live broadcast applications where latency and signal integrity are paramount.

Operational ROI

The integration of JPEG XS compression into live IP broadcast solutions offers significant operational benefits, particularly in terms of reduced transmission costs and lower latency compared to traditional satellite or fiber-based transmission methods. By compressing video signals in real-time, broadcasters can achieve bitrate reductions of up to 10:1, resulting in lower transmission costs and enabling the use of existing network infrastructure for high-quality video transport. This affects the workflow step of signal transport, where the reduced bitrate enables more efficient use of network bandwidth, simplifying signal routing and reducing the hardware rack footprint required for signal processing and transmission.

In comparison to existing approaches, the use of JPEG XS compression offers a more efficient and cost-effective solution for live IP broadcast. Traditional methods often rely on more complex and power-hungry compression algorithms, which can introduce additional latency and require more extensive hardware setups. In contrast, JPEG XS compression provides a lightweight and standardized solution that can be easily integrated into existing broadcast infrastructures, reducing the operational complexity and costs associated with signal transport and processing.

Security & Integration

The integration of JPEG XS compression into live IP broadcast solutions must be carefully considered in terms of security and compliance with relevant broadcast standards. The use of JPEG XS compression is compliant with the SMPTE ST 2110 standard, ensuring seamless integration with existing IP-based broadcast systems. Additionally, the use of standardized protocols such as NMOS (Networked Media Open Specification) for device discovery and registration, and AES67 for audio over IP, ensures that the compressed video signals can be easily transported and synchronized with audio and other metadata. From a cybersecurity perspective, the use of JPEG XS compression does not introduce any new vulnerabilities, as it is a standardized and widely adopted compression algorithm that can be easily integrated into existing security frameworks.

Engineering Takeaways

  • Deployment: The deployment of JPEG XS compression in live IP broadcast solutions requires a minimum network bandwidth of 1 GbE, with a recommended bandwidth of 10 GbE for high-quality video transport. Additionally, the use of JPEG XS compression requires compatible hardware, such as intoPIX's IP-cores or software plugins, which must be carefully selected and configured to ensure optimal performance.
  • Compatibility: The JPEG XS compression algorithm is compliant with the SMPTE ST 2110-22 standard, ensuring seamless integration with existing IP-based broadcast systems. Additionally, the use of standardized protocols such as NMOS IS-04 and AES67 ensures compatibility with a wide range of broadcast devices and systems.
  • What to Watch: Engineers should track the upcoming updates to the SMPTE ST 2110 standard, which are expected to include new specifications for JPEG XS compression and other emerging technologies. Additionally, the development of new hardware and software solutions that support JPEG XS compression will be important to monitor, as these will enable even more efficient and cost-effective live IP broadcast solutions.

The integration of JPEG XS compression into live IP broadcast solutions signals a significant shift towards more efficient and cost-effective signal transport and processing. As the broadcast industry continues to adopt IP-based technologies, engineers should prioritize the evaluation and deployment of JPEG XS compression and other emerging technologies to ensure optimal performance and compatibility in their live broadcast workflows.

Analysis: ST 2110 adoption enables efficient video transport in VFX workflows, allowing for reduced latency and increased bitrate in post-production environments, such as those used for 'The Dinosaurs' visual effects creation.
